ai2027.text: Doubling every four months or faster from 2024, continuing to shorten, is the premise of the superhuman-coder timeline.

nk.text: Capability can move fast; the paper's speed limits sit downstream of methods. A short doubling time does not contradict Normal Technology on its own.

nk.text: The 80% horizon is the number that matters for products; it should lag the 50% horizon by years because reliability fixes are application-specific.

nk.text: The capability-reliability gap stays wide (ratio of five or more); benchmarks are false summits.

card.name: Share of work hours assisted by generative AI

ai2027.text: A fifth or more of work hours assisted as agents diffuse through white-collar work.

nk.text: Single-digit share of work hours in year three, like PCs and the web at the same age.

nk.text: Under a third of firms in year three; organisational speed, not capability speed.

card.name: US businesses paying for AI (Ramp AI Index)

ai2027.text: Paid adoption keeps rising toward universality as agents pay for themselves.

capture.text: Trillions of dollars of AI revenue before 2030 (Amodei) would need paid adoption close to universal.

nk.text: Paid adoption saturates early among tech-forward firms and flattens as the hard integration work begins.

card.name: US labour productivity, year on year

predictions.claimant: Korinek et al. (The Anthropic Institute, WP 2026-02)

capture.text: Productivity growth well above trend by 2030 on the extreme path; under half a point of GDP growth on the modest one (Korinek et al.).

nk.text: Productivity at trend for years; the Solow paradox repeats (paper's entries 28, 29, 61).

card.name: US total factor productivity, private nonfarm business

predictions.claimant: Korinek et al. (The Anthropic Institute, WP 2026-02)

capture.text: TFP separates from trend only after 2027, and only on the substantial and extreme paths (Korinek et al.).

nk.text: TFP invisible at annual resolution; Acemoglu's 0.66% over a decade is the normal reading.

card.name: US labour share of income, year on year

predictions.claimant: Korinek et al. (The Anthropic Institute, WP 2026-02)

capture.text: Labour share falls from about 60% toward 45% by 2030 on the extreme path (Korinek et al.).

nk.text: Labour share moves within its cyclical range; no AI-attributable break before 2028.

card.name: Entry-level employment shortfall in AI-exposed occupations

predictions.claimant: Korinek et al. (The Anthropic Institute, WP 2026-02)

capture.text: Cognitive employment down about 4% by 2030 on the substantial path; entry-level exposed work breaks first (Korinek et al.).

nk.text: No broad AI-attributable employment decline for years; canaries stay within youth-employment swings.

predictions.claimant: Korinek et al. (The Anthropic Institute, WP 2026-02)

capture.text: On the substantial path the trackers converge on a decline in exposed occupations by 2030 (Korinek et al.).

nk.text: The four monthly labour trackers agree on a null.

card.name: Semiconductors' share of stack operating income

ai2027.text: Whoever controls the frontier labs and their compute captures a rising share as capability compounds.

capture.text: The chip layer's share of stack profit is the question the gap analyses turn on: spend far ahead of revenue (Cahn, Covello).

nk.text: Rents at a chokepoint erode as users capture most of the surplus, the usual course for a general-purpose technology.

answers: Who keeps it: Compute & physical / Hyperscalers
card.name: Hyperscaler capex to AI revenue (trailing year)

ai2027.text: Capex is repaid quickly because capability growth turns into revenue fast.

capture.text: Infrastructure spend many times AI revenue, needing revenue in the trillions to justify it (Cahn, Bain, Tunguz).

nk.text: Capex runs ahead of revenue for years, as in earlier infrastructure build-outs.

answers: Who keeps it: Model / Frontier labs
card.name: Lab recoupment ratio

ai2027.text: Lab revenue compounds fast enough to fund the next training runs from operations.

capture.text: Trillions of dollars of revenue before 2030 (Amodei) against the capital already raised.

lab.text: Revenue growing about tenfold a year (Amodei).

capture.text: Circular deals inflate reported demand and widen the gap between spend and end revenue (Cahn).

nk.text: Vendor financing is a normal feature of a build-out and unwinds as end demand is proven.
